## Objective
- Build a playable solo-character-based MOBA prototype in the browser for a ruined-city battleground, with a five-hero team, per-character logic, and direct hero switching.

## Requirements
- Five-character roster with distinct roles and abilities, balanced for solo play.
- One-vs-one-style skirmish structure, but with a five-man team under player control.
- Ability to switch control between heroes at will.
- Ruined city map and solo-compatible gameplay.
- “Bad teammates are the bane” design: player sets logic for each ally instead of relying on teammates.
- No multiplayer required for this build.
- “Build a complete, playable game now” and do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Assumed this is a single-player, AI-controlled enemy skirmish prototype rather than networked multiplayer.
- Built the initial version as a self-contained browser game in `index.html` with a UI, battlefield, hero roster, enemy wave logic, and core/tower combat loop.
- Chosen battle design: switch active hero with `1-5`, use WASD movement, SPACE attack, Q skill, and click-to-move/focus target.

- Created a browser-based playable solo MOBA prototype in `index.html`.
- Added a five-hero roster: Aelia, Teneia, Oola, Brann, and Mira.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e3f382af3ffegVX3Kih1IrfRcG" state="completed">
## Findings — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`

- **Battlefield topology — lines 12, 17, 20, 25–35, 39–49, 54–57.** The simulation uses a fixed `1400×800` world. It is essentially a single horizontal lane at `y=322–474`, with allied/enemy towers at `(175,400)` and `(1225,400)` and cores at `(78,400)` and `(1322,400)`. Four circular jungle zones are at `(420,170)`, `(480,625)`, `(930,180)`, and `(900,640)`. Teams spawn near opposite ends; periodic minion waves travel in opposite directions. Terrain is decorative: movement has world-edge clamps but no obstacle or wall collision.  
  **Suggested changes:** If walls, jungle, or lane boundaries should affect play, add collision/pathing rules; otherwise, the open movement across decorative obstacles is consistent with the current implementation.

- **Canvas sizing and coordinates — line 37; canvas CSS on line 3; pointer mapping on line 64.** `resize()` sets the canvas backing dimensions from its displayed rectangle and caps DPR at 2. It then scales X and Y independently to the world dimensions. Pointer coordinates are likewise independently mapped from the displayed rectangle to `1400×800`.  
  **Suggested changes:** If the battlefield should retain its world aspect ratio, use a uniform scale with letterboxing and apply the same viewport offset/scale in pointer mapping. Current behavior stretches the map to fit the arena, but pointer mapping remains aligned with that stretch.

- **Hero/enemy and structure drawing — lines 51–57.** `drawStructure()` renders both towers as stylized structures with health rings/bars. `drawUnit()` uses the same basic circular silhouette for heroes and enemies, differentiated mainly by color; it adds a selection ring for the active hero and a dimmed effect for stealth. Dead units are omitted. `draw()` renders the map, towers/cores, minions, heroes, enemies, projectiles, effects, and pause/game-over overlays.  
  **Suggested changes:** For stronger unit readability, give heroes and enemy types distinct shapes or role-specific markers, and consider a visible downed/respawn indicator for units whose `dead` timer is active.

- **Input handling — lines 21, 27, 62–64.** WASD/arrows move the selected hero; Space attacks; Q uses the active hero’s skill; 1–5 switch heroes; P/Escape pause. Keyboard listeners are global. A canvas `pointerdown` focuses nearby enemies, red minions, or enemy towers, otherwise sets a clamped move destination. There are no dedicated touch movement/attack controls.  
  **Suggested changes:** Add touch-friendly controls or on-screen prompts for mobile, and consider limiting keyboard shortcuts to when the game is active/focused. Pointer targeting currently does not include the enemy core.

- **Responsive/mobile UI — CSS line 4; markup lines 5–8.** At `max-width:1050px`, the right battle-report panel is hidden and the left column narrows. At `max-width:720px`, the layout becomes a vertical stack: arena first, horizontally scrollable squad cards second; the side-panel heading and map legend disappear, and HUD/footer controls shrink. The footer’s Pause button is hidden, though the arena and keyboard pause shortcut remain.  
  **Suggested changes:** Provide a visible mobile pause control and touch controls; verify the HUD and action button remain legible at narrow widths and short viewport heights.

## Objective
- Complete a playable solo browser MOBA prototype set in the ruined city of Veyra, with five switchable heroes and configurable ally logic.
- Adapt it for mobile play with three lanes, jungles between lanes, touch-compatible controls, and enemies visually distinct by role so players can judge threats.

## Requirements
- Five distinct heroes; player can switch control at will and configure ally behavior.
- Solo skirmish against an AI-controlled opposing team; no multiplayer.
- Include Aelia’s stealth/stun/frenzy, Teneia’s area root/defense, and Oola’s jungle detection/grass damage.
- Mobile UI and touch controls; three lanes with jungles between them.
- Make enemy character shapes reflect their roles rather than rendering all as indistinguishable red circles.

## Decisions
- Implement the game as a self-contained `index.html` titled “ASHEN CROWN,” set in the “Ruins of Veyra.”
- Existing desktop controls are WASD movement, SPACE attack, Q ability, 1–5 hero switching, and canvas clicks for movement or target focus.
- Squad card hero selection and ally-logic controls are separate sibling buttons.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the interface, five-hero roster, configurable squad logic, battlefield, combat simulation, abilities, minion waves, towers, cores, and win/loss handling.
- Added deployment, pause/resume, keyboard and pointer input, HUD updates, and animation loop.
- Fixed Aelia’s Q reactivation during Ghoststep and reset stale movement/target focus on redeploy.
- Fixed squad card markup so logic changes do not switch the active hero; verified both controls.
- Added initial CSS for mobile touch controls and compact mobile layout, and added joystick/attack/skill control markup.
- Added a lane coordinate array and began adjusting hero spawn positions for the mid lane.

### Active
- Replace the single-lane battlefield with three lanes and jungles between them; the attempted `drawMap()` edit failed because its exact source text did not match.
- Complete functional on-screen joystick, attack, and skill controls.
- Render enemy role silhouettes/shapes so enemy threats are identifiable.
- Test mobile layout and gameplay after changes.

### Blocked
- `(none)`

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `index.html` to confirm the partial mobile CSS, controls markup, and lane/spawn edits.
2. Update `drawMap()` to draw three lanes using `world.lanes`, then align spawns, structures, minion waves, AI lane behavior, and jungle zones with the new topology.
3. Add working joystick input and touch attack/skill handlers.
4. Update `drawUnit()` with clear role-based enemy shapes and labels/indicators.
5. Run syntax checks and browser tests at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

- `index.html`: self-contained game, rendering, simulation, UI, and input implementation.

- Earlier headless Chromium checks passed for deployment, Aelia’s two-stage ability, Teneia’s ability, hero switching, pause/resume, victory/defeat, and redeploy, with no runtime errors.
- Existing world dimensions are `1400×800`; old simulation assumes a single horizontal lane centered around `y=400`.
- Recent lane-map patch did not apply; no three-lane battlefield drawing change has been completed yet.
- Changes are uncommitted; repository contains several untracked files, including `index.html`.

## Objective
- Complete the solo browser MOBA prototype set in the ruined city of Veyra as a touch-compatible mobile game with three lanes, intervening jungles, and enemies visually distinguishable by role.

## Requirements
- Five switchable heroes with configurable ally logic; solo play against an AI team, no multiplayer.
- Preserve Aelia’s stealth/stun/frenzy, Teneia’s area root/defense, and Oola’s jungle detection/grass damage.
- Mobile UI and touch controls; three lanes with jungles between them.
- Give enemies visually distinct role-based shapes so players can assess threats.

## Decisions
- Keep the game self-contained in `index.html`, titled “ASHEN CROWN — Ruins of Veyra.”
- Retain desktop controls: WASD, SPACE, Q, 1–5, and canvas clicks.
- Keep hero selection and ally-logic controls as separate sibling buttons.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added mobile-responsive layout and joystick/attack/skill control markup; connected touch movement to active-hero movement.
- Added three lanes at y-coordinates 165, 400, and 635, jungle zones between lanes, and allied/enemy towers in each lane.
- Updated hero/enemy spawns, lane-specific enemy targeting, minion waves and combat, lane-specific tower targeting, and victory check to account for all enemy towers.

### Active
- Finish and verify lane topology integration, including allied core access and per-lane structure progression; review remaining tower/minion targeting assumptions.
- Implement touch joystick, attack, and skill handlers; markup and movement state exist, but handler insertion previously failed.
- Draw role-specific enemy silhouettes/indicators for tank, marksman, assassin, support, and fighter.
- Test mobile layout and gameplay; run syntax and browser checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining lane/core progression and tower logic in `index.html`; fix any single-lane assumptions.
2. Add joystick pointer handling, touch attack press/release, and touch skill activation.
3. Render distinct role-based enemy shapes and indicators.
4. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests, then fix regressions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game UI, map, simulation, rendering, and controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` was previously untracked.
- Earlier browser checks passed deployment, abilities, hero switching, pause/resume, win/loss, and redeploy before the current mobile/three-lane edits.
- Latest edits updated lane assignment during movement, lane-filtered minion combat and tower targets, and required all enemy towers destroyed for victory.
